requirement.evidence: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
requirement.note: Other elements (cure notice for at-fault, no-fault causes, 3 months relocation or rent waiver) are also stated in the document.

key_value.evidence: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

coverage.evidence: The Just Cause Ordinance shall not apply to certain types of residential property, including housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
coverage.note: The 15-year exemption is supported, but the card omits the other exemptions (deed-restricted, hotel, hospital, dormitories, etc.).

citation.evidence: a Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, which limits the allowed reasons for which a renter can be evicted.
citation.note: The ordinance is named in the document, but no section or ordinance number is given.

requirement.evidence: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
requirement.note: Publication by June 30, effective September 1, and written notice requirement are also stated.
